campaign_id: qwen35-9b-w4a16 depth sweep d4/d5/d6 vs published w1 (2026-09-07, one B70)
question: Whether MTP depth 3 is right for the W4A16 route or was inherited from the FP8 route's sweep. There was a specific reason to expect a different answer: on FP8, depths 4, 5 and 6 were each repeat-exact but diverged from the MTP0 oracle on a third of the suite. A verify step at depth d processes d+1 rows, so depth changes the GEMM's row count - the same dependence that makes the FP8 route flip near-tie tokens as concurrency changes. The W4A16 kernel is row-count invariant, so deeper drafts should stay lossless.
finding: Every depth from 3 to 6 is lossless on this route: G1, G2 and both G3 comparisons matched 12/12 at all four depths. On FP8 only depth 3 did. The prediction held, on an axis independent of the one it was derived from - depth changes the verify step's row count without changing the number of concurrent users - so FP8's loss of identity above depth 3 was not a property of speculative decoding but of the row-count dependence its GEMM has and this one does not.
speed: Throughput falls monotonically with depth: 113.63/112.90 at depth 3, 108.45/108.24 at 4, 104.91/104.85 at 5, 99.27/99.32 at 6. Depth 3 is confirmed as the operating point, now on this route's own evidence rather than inherited. No speed was being left unclaimed.
